From 641f6fda143b879da1515f821ee475073678cf2a Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Mukesh Ojha <mukesh.ojha@oss.qualcomm.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Jan 2026 20:53:20 +0530
Subject: [PATCH] soc: qcom: pd-mapper: Fix element length in
 servreg_loc_pfr_req_ei

It looks element length declared in servreg_loc_pfr_req_ei for reason
not matching servreg_loc_pfr_req's reason field due which we could
observe decoding error on PD crash.

  qmi_decode_string_elem: String len 81 >= Max Len 65

Fix this by matching with servreg_loc_pfr_req's reason field.

Fixes: 1ebcde047c54 ("soc: qcom: add pd-mapper implementation")
Signed-off-by: Mukesh Ojha <mukesh.ojha@oss.qualcomm.com>
Reviewed-by: Dmitry Baryshkov <dmitry.baryshkov@oss.qualcomm.com>
Tested-by: Nikita Travkin <nikita@trvn.ru>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20260129152320.3658053-2-mukesh.ojha@oss.qualcomm.com
Signed-off-by: Bjorn Andersson <andersson@kernel.org>

diff --git a/drivers/soc/qcom/pdr_internal.h b/drivers/soc/qcom/pdr_internal.h
index 039508c1bbf7..047c0160b617 100644
--- a/drivers/soc/qcom/pdr_internal.h
+++ b/drivers/soc/qcom/pdr_internal.h
@@ -84,7 +84,7 @@ struct servreg_set_ack_resp {
 
 struct servreg_loc_pfr_req {
 	char service[SERVREG_NAME_LENGTH + 1];
-	char reason[257];
+	char reason[SERVREG_PFR_LENGTH + 1];
 };
 
 struct servreg_loc_pfr_resp {

diff --git a/drivers/soc/qcom/qcom_pdr_msg.c b/drivers/soc/qcom/qcom_pdr_msg.c
index ca98932140d8..02022b11ecf0 100644
--- a/drivers/soc/qcom/qcom_pdr_msg.c
+++ b/drivers/soc/qcom/qcom_pdr_msg.c
@@ -325,7 +325,7 @@ const struct qmi_elem_info servreg_loc_pfr_req_ei[] = {
 	},
 	{
 		.data_type = QMI_STRING,
-		.elem_len = SERVREG_NAME_LENGTH + 1,
+		.elem_len = SERVREG_PFR_LENGTH + 1,
 		.elem_size = sizeof(char),
 		.array_type = VAR_LEN_ARRAY,
 		.tlv_type = 0x02,

diff --git a/include/linux/soc/qcom/pdr.h b/include/linux/soc/qcom/pdr.h
index 83a8ea612e69..2b7691e47c2a 100644
--- a/include/linux/soc/qcom/pdr.h
+++ b/include/linux/soc/qcom/pdr.h
@@ -5,6 +5,7 @@
 #include <linux/soc/qcom/qmi.h>
 
 #define SERVREG_NAME_LENGTH	64
+#define SERVREG_PFR_LENGTH	256
 
 struct pdr_service;
 struct pdr_handle;
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary of Modifications

### Files Modified

1. **`drivers/soc/qcom/pdr_internal.h`**  
   - Changed the `reason` field in `struct servreg_loc_pfr_req` from `char reason[257]` to `char reason[SERVREG_PFR_LENGTH + 1]`.  
   - This aligns the struct definition with the new constant `SERVREG_PFR_LENGTH` (defined in the header below).

2. **`drivers/soc/qcom/qcom_pdr_msg.c`**  
   - In the `servreg_loc_pfr_req_ei[]` array, fixed the `elem_len` of the second element (representing the `reason` field) from `SERVREG_NAME_LENGTH + 1` (65) to `SERVREG_PFR_LENGTH + 1` (257).  
   - This corrects the mismatch that caused decoding errors (e.g., `String len 81 >= Max Len 65`).

3. **`include/linux/soc/qcom/pdr.h`**  
   - Added a new macro `SERVREG_PFR_LENGTH` defined as `256`.  
   - This macro is used by the other two files to consistently represent the correct maximum length of the `reason` field.

### Relationships Between Modifications

- **Root cause**: The struct `servreg_loc_pfr_req` declared `reason` as `char[257]`, but the QMI element info incorrectly specified its maximum length as `SERVREG_NAME_LENGTH + 1` (= 65). This mismatch caused QMI decoding to fail when the received string exceeded 65 characters.
- **Fix approach**: Introduce a dedicated constant `SERVREG_PFR_LENGTH` (set to 256) to represent the true allowed length of the `reason` field. Then update both the struct definition and the QMI element info to reference this constant, ensuring consistency.
- **Dependencies**:
  - `pdr.h` provides the new constant `SERVREG_PFR_LENGTH`.
  - `pdr_internal.h` uses it to define the struct field.
  - `qcom_pdr_msg.c` uses it to set the correct `elem_len` in the QMI element descriptor.

The mismatch caused a decoding error when the reason string exceeded 65 bytes. The fix introduces a proper constant for the maximum length and updates all relevant definitions.

   - Added a new macro `SERVREG_PFR_LENGTH` with value `256` to define the maximum length of the `reason` field in the PFR (Power Failure Reason) request.

   - In `servreg_loc_pfr_req_ei` (the QMI element info array), updated the `elem_len` for the `reason` element from `SERVREG_NAME_LENGTH + 1` (which was 65) to `SERVREG_PFR_LENGTH + 1` (which is 257). This makes the expected QMI element length match the actual buffer size in the struct, preventing the decoding error.

### Relationship between changes:
- The constant `SERVREG_PFR_LENGTH` serves as the single source of truth for the size of the `reason` field. Both the struct definition and the QMI element info now use this constant, ensuring consistency.
- The previous code used `SERVREG_NAME_LENGTH` (65) for the QMI element length, which was incorrect for the larger `reason` field (257 bytes). The fix corrects this by introducing a dedicated constant and applying it in both places.

## Summary of Modifications

The patch fixes a mismatch between the QMI element length and the actual buffer size of the `reason` field in `servreg_loc_pfr_req`, which caused decoding errors. The fix aligns these definitions by introducing a new constant.

### Modifications per file

1. **`include/linux/soc/qcom/pdr.h`**  
   - Added a new macro: `#define SERVREG_PFR_LENGTH 256` to represent the correct length for the "reason" field (instead of incorrectly reusing `SERVREG_NAME_LENGTH`).

2. **`drivers/soc/qcom/pdr_internal.h`**  
   - Changed the `reason` array size in `struct servreg_loc_pfr_req` from hardcoded `257` to `SERVREG_PFR_LENGTH + 1` (i.e., `257` remains the same value, but now derived from the new macro to ensure consistency).

3. **`drivers/soc/qcom/qcom_pdr_msg.c`**  
   - Updated the `.elem_len` field of the second entry in `servreg_loc_pfr_req_ei[]` from `SERVREG_NAME_LENGTH + 1` (which was `65`) to `SERVREG_PFR_LENGTH + 1` (which is `257`), matching the actual buffer size.

### Relationships between the changes

- The root cause was that the QMI element descriptor declared a maximum string length of `65` (based on `SERVREG_NAME_LENGTH`), while the actual buffer in the struct was `257` bytes. This caused the QMI decoder to reject strings longer than 65 characters.
- The new macro `SERVREG_PFR_LENGTH` (value `256`) is defined in the public header and used in both:
  - The struct definition (buffer size), and
  - The QMI element descriptor (allowed string length).
- By using the same macro in both places, the buffer size and the declared element length are now identical, eliminating the decoding error.
